sentences.text: The original description relied on an incomplete snout and an articulated lower jaw.
This animal is classified as a reptile.
Arthur Smith Woodward first described the genus in 1896.
It was the first non-Cenozoic sebecosuchian to be described by this researcher.
Cynodontosuchus belongs to the family Baurusuchidae.
Some researchers suggest it is a senior synonym of the genus Baurusuchus.
It differs from Baurusuchus by having a shallower rostrum and five maxillary teeth.
Remains from Argentina come from the Bajo de la Carpa Formation and the Pichi Picun Leufu Formation.
Fossils have also been found in the Tiupampan Santa Lucía Formation of Bolivia.
The creature lived between 85.7 and 61.66 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to the Danian.
